Nectar Lifesciences Ltd. Buyback (Nectar Lifesciences Buyback 2025) Detail

Tender Offer | ₹81.00 Crores | Listed at BSE, NSE | Wed, Dec 31, 2025 - Tue, Jan 6, 2026

Buyback Detail
Messages
Docs
News
FAQs

Nectar Lifesciences Ltd. Buyback is a tender offer for the repurchase of up to 3.00 crore equity shares, representing 13.38% of the total paid-up equity share capital at a buyback price of ₹27 per share with a face value of ₹1 per share, aggregating to ₹81.00 crores.

The record date for determining eligible shareholders is Dec 24, 2025. Shareholders holding equity shares as on the record date are eligible to participate in the buyback.

The buyback opens on Dec 31, 2025 and closes on Jan 6, 2026, with the last date for receipt of tender forms being Jan 6, 2026.

The finalisation of buyback acceptance is expected on Jan 12, 2026, followed by settlement of bids on Jan 13, 2026.

Master Capital Services Ltd. is the Manager to the Buyback and Kfin Technologies Ltd. is the Registrar and Master Capital Service Limited is the Registered Broker to the Buyback.

Investors are advised to refer to the Nectar Lifesciences Ltd. Letter of Offer for detailed information, including eligibility criteria, entitlement ratio, acceptance methodology, and tax implications.

About Nectar Lifesciences Ltd.

Nectar Lifesciences is a research-driven, fully integrated pharmaceutical company. Its core business revolves around manufacturing Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) — especially cephalosporin antibiotics — as well as intermediates.

Beyond APIs, the company also produces finished dosage forms (FDFs / formulations) — such as tablets, capsules, suspensions, granules, and injectables — through contract manufacturing. They also manufacture empty hard gelatin capsules (EHGCs) and have a presence in phytochemicals / menthol-based products.

Nectar has multiple state-of-the-art manufacturing facilities: 13 facilities across Punjab and Himachal Pradesh (oral and sterile drug production, empty capsule production, menthol/phytochemicals).

The plants are compliant with global regulatory standards (cGMP / EHS) and have approvals from international regulatory authorities (for export markets) — underscoring their quality assurance.

Necessity of the Issue

  • The buyback will help the company to return surplus cash to its shareholders holding equity shares broadly in proportion to their shareholding, thereby, enhancing the overall return to shareholders.
  • The buyback will help the company to optimize the capital structure;
  • The Buyback, which is being implemented through the Tender Offer route as prescribed under the SEBI Buyback Regulations, would involve allocation of the number of equity shares as per their entitlement or 15% of the number of equity shares to be bought back, whichever is higher, reserved. The company believes that the reservation for small shareholders would benefit a large number of the Company's public shareholders, who get classified as "Small Shareholders, as per regulations 2(i)(n) of the SEBI Buyback Regulations.
  • The buyback may help in improving financial ratios like earnings per share, return on capital employed, and return on equity, by reduction in the equity base, thereby leading to long-term increase in shareholders' vlaue; and
  • The buyback gives an option to the shareholders holding Equity shares of the company, who can choose to participate and get cash in lieu of Equity shares to be accepted under the Buyback offer or they may choose not to participate and enjoy a resultant increase in their percentage shareholding, post the buyback offer, without additional investment.

Letter of Offer

All the eligible Shareholders of the Company holding either Physical Shares or Demat Shares as on the Record Date can participate in the buyback offer through their Stock Broker.

The eligible shareholder holding the shares in Demat form needs to inform their broker the details of the Equity shares they wish to tender in the Buyback Offer. The shareholder needs to transfer the tendered shares to a Special account of the clearing corporation. The broker, in turn, would place an order on the stock exchange for the buyback.

The eligible shareholder holding the shares in physical form needs to approach their broker with original share certificates and supporting documents. Upon completion of document verification, the broker places an order on the stock exchange and submits the original share certificate and TRS to the registrar.

The tender form and TRS are optional in the case of Demat shares but mandatory in the case of physical shares.

The Nectar Lifesciences Buyback 2025 offers an opportunity for the shareholders to exit their positions at a premium price. In case you stay invested you would have an increased percentage of shareholding in the company and improved earnings per share. Thus, one should understand the company fundamentals along with one's need, goals, and risk appetite to decide if one wants to stay invested or participate in the buyback offer.
